Your servers,
one handshake away.

HandSSHake is a desktop SSH client for Linux and macOS, written in Go. Save every host once, then connect in a click — with a built-in terminal, SFTP, key management, and an encrypted vault that never leaves your device.

  • Latest release · v1.3.1
  • Linux & macOS
  • Credentials stay on-device
  • Open source
terminal — install One-click install
$curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orchid0610/handsshake/main/install.sh | bash

Paste it in any terminal. The script detects your OS, downloads the latest release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and installs it — a .deb on Debian/Ubuntu, a tarball elsewhere on Linux, and the .app on macOS. Preview first with --dry-run.

Everything you need to live in SSH

No more digging through ~/.ssh/config or retyping passwords. HandSSHake keeps your hosts, keys and sessions in one calm, fast desktop app.

Saved hosts, zero friction

Every server saved as a card with its OS, user and address. Search by name, hostname or IP (Ctrl K), import existing connections, and pick up recent sessions right where you left off.

A real built-in terminal

Full SSH sessions inside the app — no juggling terminal windows. Themes, fonts and density apply instantly to every open session, with a live preview while you tune them.

Encrypted vault

Your hosts, passwords and keys sit behind a master password in an encrypted vault. Forgot it? A recovery key gets you back in. Credentials are encrypted and stored only on this device — nothing is synced anywhere.

SSH key management

A dedicated Keys section keeps your SSH keys organized alongside your hosts, so the right key is always attached to the right connection — no more hunting through folders.

SFTP built in

Move files to and from your servers without leaving the app or opening a second tool. Browse and transfer over the same secure connection as your terminal session.

Made to be tuned

Four terminal themes, JetBrains Mono or your system mono, font size and line-height sliders — a workspace that looks the way you think, on Linux and macOS alike.

See it in action

Real screens from the app — the hosts list you land on, the terminal settings, and the vault that guards it all.

Your hosts

Connect to and manage your secure servers. Search, import, add a host, and resume recent sessions in one click.

A terminal that feels like yours

HandSSHake ships with four hand-picked terminal themes and live font controls. Try the themes here — the preview reacts just like it does in the app.

Typography too: JetBrains Mono or system mono, with font-size and line-height sliders — applied instantly to all terminal sessions.

Install in under a minute

One command, both platforms. The installer is a plain bash script you can read before you run it — and every download is checksum-verified before anything is installed.

  1. 1

    Run the one-liner

    Copy the command at the top of this page into your terminal. Add --dry-run to preview every step without changing anything.

  2. 2

    It detects, downloads & verifies

    Linux gets the .deb on Debian/Ubuntu or the tarball in ~/.local/bin on other distros. macOS gets the universal HandSSHake.app — Apple Silicon and Intel in one build — installed to /Applications.

  3. 3

    Set a master password & connect

    Launch HandSSHake, create your vault, add or import your first host, and click Connect. Changing your mind later is one flag: --uninstall removes the app and keeps your hosts and settings.

Prefer a direct download?

Latest release v1.3.1 from GitHub — same files the installer fetches.

macOS — Universalhandsshake-macos-universal.zip · Apple Silicon + Intel Linux — Debian / Ubuntuhandsshake-linux-amd64.deb · x86_64 Linux — Any distrohandsshake-linux-amd64.tar.gz · needs GTK 3 + WebKitGTK 4.1

Installer options, after bash -s --:

  • --version v1.3.1 — pin a specific release
  • --dry-run — show what would happen, change nothing
  • --uninstall — remove the app, keep your data

Every release ships a SHA256SUMS.txt, and the installer refuses to install anything whose checksum doesn't match.
